description: The cell rationale flags that MK and EN NBRSM pages can carry different granularity, but with both pages returning 403 the MK-vs-EN table inventory could not be compared.

The actual XLSX/PDF payment-statistics table URLs (per-terminal-type transactions, POS card value, cards issued) were never enumerated because the parent pages are bot-blocked; only a naming pattern (/WBStorage/Files/Platni sistemi_*) and one historical example were observed.

KIBS AD Skopje (the clearing house operating the retail net-settlement system) was reached only through the central bank's description page; its own corporate site and volume statistics were not searched in this cell.

No advance release calendar for the payment statistics was captured, only the general rule (quarterly within 90 days of quarter end, annual within 90 days of year end) reported for the payment statistics page.
Depth of the back-series for card/ATM/POS statistics (earliest available year, methodological breaks) is unknown; a 2019 monetary-statistics change note was seen, implying breaks exist elsewhere too.

No register specifically enumerating licensed payment institutions and e-money issuers was located within this cell; the Central Registry lists legal entities generically and the licensing register is held by the central bank.
Most UJP and Central Registry material is Macedonian-only; English mirrors exist for SSO but were not systematically compared for content parity.
SSO household budget survey (Анкета за потрошувачка на домаќинствата) and its treatment of cash vs non-cash expenditure was not examined in this pass.

The Bureau for Public Procurement e-procurement system (e-nabavki), which would reveal bank/POS/ATM vendor contracts, falls outside this cell's four institutions but is adjacent to the Open Finance portal captured here.

Merchant-side sector bodies beyond the generic Trade Association are unmapped: no located association for supermarkets/FMCG retail chains, petrol retail, or hospitality with its own publication stream.
Albanian-language association and chamber content was not searched at all.

Member lists were located as URLs (MBA /clenovi/, MASIT /members-of-masit/) but not extracted into an actor registry, and several bodies (chamber associations, BCM, chamber.mk) may not publish machine-readable member lists at all.

Association-produced surveys with numbers are thin — only the e-commerce association clearly publishes payment-preference survey content. No association-run merchant or consumer survey on cash vs card was otherwise found.
Only a 2018 edition of the Foreign Investors Council White Book was observed, and chamber annual reports were seen for scattered years (2010, 2020, 2022).

Consumer grievance signal is richest where it is least collectible — ОПМ's complaint intake is a submission form (must not be interacted with) and its most active channel is Facebook, which is login-walled and ToS-restricted.

All identified outlets are Skopje-centric national media. No regional MK outlets (Bitola, Kumanovo, Tetovo, Ohrid, Štip) were identified, yet branch/ATM withdrawal is a rural and secondary-city phenomenon first.

No merchant-side or consumer-association voice was located — no retail association, chamber of commerce media channel, or consumer-protection organisation covering card acceptance costs and interchange complaints.
No paywalled/print archive access was established for the business weeklies (Kapital print edition, Fokus), so pre-web and subscriber-only reporting is out of reach.
No URL in this slice was fetched; all were obtained from search-result metadata. Liveness, paywall state, robots.txt and feed availability are unverified.

Broadcast and social-first channels are underrepresented: only Telma and Alsat were captured, and no YouTube/Facebook broadcast archives were assessed, though MK banking executives frequently make first statements in TV interviews.
Primary career pages of the ~13 MK banks, plus CaSys, KIBS, Diners Club MK, Paysera MK and the payment institutions/e-money institutions registered with NBRSM, are not enumerated.
The MK functional vocabulary for payments roles is only partially assembled (картично работење, платен промет, банкомати, самоуслужни производи, платежни решенија, засилена автентикација).
Albanian-language sources not covered.
No archival strategy identified for vacancy text, which is deleted once a post expires — the signal is perishable.
Event agendas and speaker lists were identified at organiser level but no past-edition agenda was actually retrieved, so the speaker-to-institution map is unbuilt.
Vendor-side signals for the ATM/POS supply chain (Payten, Printec, Diebold/NCR partners, ASSECO SEE in MK) were not located — the vendor query returned only Nextsense.
LinkedIn — the richest layer — is not lawfully pipelineable, and e-Rabota is an ASP.NET postback form that resists simple crawling.

No card-processing or ATM-operating infrastructure actor was captured (e.g. the national card processor, the interbank clearing operator, independent ATM deployers, or the banking association), all of which hold ATM/POS estate data not visible in central-bank aggregates.
Primary Official Gazette texts for the AML cash ceiling and for the Law on Registration of Cash Payments were not obtained.

No source was found that directly reports the cash share of retail transactions (as opposed to cash withdrawals or currency in circulation). Media report qualitatively that cash is still preferred, and NBRM data support an ATM-withdrawal-to-POS-purchase ratio, but no survey-based cash-share series surfaced.
ATM network density is available only at national level (per 100k adults). No municipality- or region-level ATM/POS distribution source was identified.
The Finance Think homepage URL was inferred from the institute's name rather than observed in a search result, unlike every other candidate URL in this slice.

Card-scheme and payments-industry research (Visa, Mastercard, Worldpay/FIS Global Payments Report, Nilson Report, Euromonitor Consumer Finance) was not searched; these vendors publish MK or Southeast-Europe card-volume and payment-mix estimates that are the closest commercial analogue to official card statistics.
BIS CPMI Red Book / CPMI statistics and EBRD outputs (Transition Report, Banking Environment and Performance Survey) were not reached before the search budget ran out.

The Wayback CDX enumeration was run only for nbrm.mk with a 'platni' filter and a 25-row limit. The same technique has not been applied to nbstat.nbrm.mk, stat.gov.mk, the nine MK commercial bank domains, KIBS (the domestic clearing house), or the MK card-scheme/processor sites, and no 'karti'/'tarif'/'statistik' filters were run against nbrm.mk itself.

Only the Internet Archive was used. Other preservation routes — archive.today/archive.ph, Common Crawl, Bing/Google cache, national or library web archives, and the EU/Europeana web-archiving initiatives — were not tested for MK banking pages.

For every paid aggregator in this cell (CEIC, Trading Economics, Statista, Mordor/ResearchAndMarkets, bne IntelliNews, TheBanks.eu) it is unknown whether the organisation already holds a subscription, which determines whether these become collectable sources or stay reference-only.

No comparator peer group has been fixed for MK. ECB PAY, World Bank and IMF FAS all allow arbitrary country selections, but without an agreed peer set (WB6 neighbours vs recent EU entrants vs euro-area small states) benchmark outputs will not be reproducible across runs.
Airlines and travel merchants operating in MK (carriers selling MKD-denominated tickets, Skopje/Ohrid airport operator TAV) were not searched.
Marketplaces and delivery/on-demand platforms (pazar3.mk, grouper.mk, Glovo/Wolt MK) are absent — these are the highest-frequency card-not-present merchants in the country.
No systematic mechanism yet defined for detecting acquirer/gateway from checkout redirects across the MK webshop population.
Municipal utilities outside Skopje and Prilep (топлификација, комунални претпријатија in Bitola, Tetovo, Kumanovo, Ohrid) and their card-payment portals are unmapped.
Albanian-language acceptance sources not covered.
nbrm.mk is bot-defended (403 to plain fetchers), and it hosts the majority of the primary sources in this cell.
The payment institution register and payment system operator register pages were identified only via the hub page; their direct URLs were not confirmed (only the e-money register URL was).
Interchange / merchant service charge regulation in MK is unresolved: term exists in law ('заменски надоместок') but no cap instrument or competition-authority decision found.
Instant payments coverage rests on media and EU/EPC sources; no primary domestic scheme documentation captured.
Albanian-language sources were not searched, although Albanian is an official language in North Macedonia and some regulatory content is published in it.
No court/administrative-enforcement source (sanctions, licence withdrawals, misdemeanour proceedings under the PSPS or AML law) was identified.
CPV codes for ATMs/banking machinery, payment terminals, card personalisation, cash-in-transit and core banking software were not established in this pass.

State-owned and state-influenced financial institutions beyond Пошта were not individually enumerated — notably Развојна банка на Северна Македонија (MBDP/development bank), the Treasury (Трезор) within the Ministry of Finance, Фонд за здравствено осигурување (ФЗОМ) and Фонд за ПИОМ, all of which run mass disbursement/collection and card-related procurement.

Municipal-level contracting authorities (80+ општини, plus the City of Skopje) were treated collectively rather than individually. Municipal cash desks, parking payment machines and local utility collection are a meaningful slice of cash/card acceptance procurement.

Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, although Albanian is an official language and audit/procurement bodies publish bilingually (the State Audit Office brands itself Enti Shtetëror i Revizionit).
No machine-readable API into ЕСЈН was identified; the collection plan currently depends on browser automation or on third-party normalisation (Opentender/TED), each with coverage or licence limits.
Historical depth of ЕСЈН public access (how far back notices and awards remain retrievable) is unknown, as is whether pre-2019-law records are comparable after the 2019 Law on Public Procurement.
Licence and terms-of-service position not resolved for two collection routes: Opentender's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial licence, and the commercial aggregators' scraping terms.

Several plausible supranational actors in this cell were not searched in this pass: EIB / EIB Global, BIS (CPMI Red Book and statistics, likely non-member so probably absent), UNCDF, USAID/SIDA/SECO bilateral donors, the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF) project pipeline, and the Vienna Initiative / EFSE and Green for Growth funds.
It was not established whether Findex 2025 country-level microdata for MK is openly downloadable or requires a licensed-access request, nor whether the MK sample supports card/POS-level breakdowns.
Albanian-language coverage (a significant official language in MK) was entirely outside the run's declared language set and was not attempted for donor/EU material.
The concrete machine-access paths for IMF FAS (post-migration data.imf.org SDMX endpoints) and for the TED search API were not tested, only inferred.

Капитал банка АД Скопје was named in a search but no reports page or filing repository was confirmed for it in this run; likewise no source was established for any remaining small/savings institutions ('штедилници') outside the main bank list.
Absolute card/ATM/POS fleet counts per bank remain unsourced; bank disclosures give growth percentages and narrative only.

English-language versions of MK bank annual reports were confirmed only for Sparkasse (historic), ProCredit and NLB Group. For Комерцијална, Стопанска, УНИ, ТТК, ЦКБ and Халк the operative documents are Macedonian Cyrillic PDFs, some of which appear to be scans.

SEI-Net and SRIS both serve documents from opaque ID-keyed endpoints (FileServer.aspx?file=<id>, Document_SR<id>-<year>-<seq>.pdf); no listing API or per-issuer index URL was established, so systematic harvesting is not yet specified.

Only recent report years (roughly 2019-2025) were sighted on live bank pages; older annual reports (e.g. Комерцијална 2016, Sparkasse 2013) surfaced only incidentally, suggesting banks prune their reports pages.

Parent-group disclosure was established for NLB Group and ProCredit Holding only. Halkbank Turkey (parent of Халкбанк АД Скопје), Steiermärkische Bank und Sparkassen AG (parent of Шпаркасе), OTP/NBG lineage for Стопанска банка and the Bulgarian CCB parent of ЦКБ were not searched at group level.
Tariff sources located for roughly 10 of the ~13 MK banks; Silk Road Bank, Ziraat Bank and Development Bank of NM remain uncovered, and savings houses (штедилници) were not scouted at all.

Merchant-side documents (acquiring general terms, POS terms of use, e-commerce merchant agreements) were found only for Stopanska banka; equivalents from NLB, Komercijalna, Halkbank and UNIBanka were not located.
Most banks expose only the currently effective tariff; historical versions were observed only for Sparkasse and CCB. Without back-versions, fee time series must be built forward from now.

Key regulator and aggregator hosts (nbrm.mk, provizii.mk) block plain HTTP fetching, and most bank tariff PDFs use long URL-encoded Cyrillic filenames that change with each revision, so static URL lists will rot quickly.
English-language versions of MK bank tariffs were not systematically checked; several banks publish EN tariff extracts which are easier to parse but may be abridged or stale.
Non-bank payment institutions, e-money institutions and independent ATM deployers / cash-in-transit or exchange-office cash access pricing are entirely absent from the current candidate set.

Because nbrm.mk .nspx pages 403 to a plain fetcher, the exact download URLs, file formats (Excel vs PDF) and update cadence of the payment-statistics tables could not be confirmed in this pass — only their landing-page URLs.

Independent/non-bank acquirers, PSPs, ATM-network operators (including any independent ATM deployers) and terminal vendors serving MK were not enumerated. The cell focused on the switch/clearing layer and did not reach the acquiring-service and terminal-estate layer, which is where POS-count intelligence actually lives.

No supranational comparative payment-statistics source for MK was captured — ECB Payment Statistics / Blue Book style datasets, World Bank Global Findex, BIS CPMI Red Book, or IMF Financial Access Survey were not searched in this pass.

The 'cash usage' topic was only touched indirectly (cashless growth percentages quoted in press). No source specific to currency in circulation, cash withdrawal volumes at ATMs, or cash-in-transit / cash-cycle actors was identified within this cell.

Several of the highest-value items are PDF series (NBRM annual payments reports, MIPS self-assessments, KIBS regulatory PDFs) whose URLs are long, percent-encoded and Cyrillic — fragile across site redesigns. No archive/mirror source (web.archive.org captures) was established.

Albanian-language sources were not searched. Albanian is widely used in North Macedonia and some institutional sites (including the Central Registry, which served an /sq/ path in results) publish Albanian versions that occasionally carry differently-timed or differently-worded content.

The full licensed population of payment institutions, e-money institutions and payment-system operators in MK is not enumerated — only two EMIs (Paysera Македонија, Iute Pay) are known by name from press.

Non-bank exchange offices (менувачници) and financial companies (финансиски друштва) that act as remittance and cash-handling nodes were only partially covered — UFS was found, but no register of exchange offices or financial companies was located.
No source found that separates non-bank PSP/EMI transaction volumes from bank-channel volumes; NBRSM card/e-commerce statistics and AETM analyses appear to report the aggregate.
Agent/branch-level geographic footprint of cash-out points (WU/MoneyGram/Ria agents, UFS agencies, bank branches) is not consolidated anywhere found.
Albanian-language sources were not searched, although a large share of MK remittance-receiving households are Albanian-speaking and some agent networks and fintech marketing are Albanian-language.
The MK importer/distributor tier for POS terminal hardware (Ingenico/Verifone/PAX/Newland/Castles) is unmapped.

No official company-registry source was reached in this pass (Централен регистар на Република Северна Македонија), which would give authoritative legal names, activity codes and annual accounts for every vendor in this cell.
Several MK cash-handling and security firms (Nikob, Perpetum Mobile) were reached only via chamber profiles or press articles, not their own domains.
Core-banking and cards-software vendors beyond Asseco SEE (e.g. Oracle FSS, Temenos, Comtrade/CT Computers, Ultra, Seavus successors, Halcom for payments) are not yet evidenced for MK banks.
Albanian-language sources were not searched, although Albanian is widely used in MK and some vendors/banks (e.g. TTK, Silk Road, Ziraat) communicate in it.
